docs.text: GroomKit for AutoDesk Maya Documentation Specialized 3D Grooming & Procedural Hair Plugin for XGen (Maya 2027+) Introduction GroomKit is an all-in-one 3D grooming toolkit designed to streamline Maya XGen styling , procedural hair generation, and advanced curve-guide control for character artists. By building on the native XGen Core engine and addressing common grooming bottlenecks, GroomKit makes creating realistic, strand-based hair much more approachable. The plugin consolidates the complex Maya grooming workflow into a compact, intuitive interface, minimizing the need to jump between menus and helping Groom Artists stay focused on the creative styling process. Key Features GroomKit Profiles: Generate and manage real-time hair Cards, Tubes, Twists, Curls, and complex Braids dynamically. Adjust length, width spans, coils, and UVs procedurally. Interactive Curve Tools: An extensive set of unified curve-guide brushes (Draw Append, Draw Cut, Draw Edit , and Geometry Shaping) controlled via interactive mouse gestures for intuitive hair sculpting. XGen Guides Binding: Bind XGen guides or Maya curves to lattices and procedural geometry. Compensate guide length, sync changes, and non-destructively shape your grooming setups. XGen Live Mirror: Enable dynamic X-axis symmetry in real-time as you sculpt and place XGen guides across your character's mesh. Painting & Masking: A detachable palette window that makes changing brush profiles, toggling mirror painting, generating XGen clumping maps, and color-flooding accessible with a double-click. Shader Presets: Apply hair shader presets to multiple descriptions with a single click, or save/load your own custom look-dev presets locally to speed up rendering pipelines. Extended Hotkeys: A clean interface for GroomKit commands, including an auto-register button to set up your custom grooming hotkeys instantly. Reusable Snippets: Utility tools that automate frequent XGen grooming tasks, such as region mapping, duplicating descriptions, and transferring mesh positions. SeExpr Expressions: Fully customizable, UI-driven SeExpr snippets (Random Wind, Random Cut) that allow you to preview, replace, and create advanced XGen modifiers with a single click. Simulation Shaping: A unified gravity draping interface that works across standard Maya curves, XGen guides, and GroomKit Profile geometry. And more! docs.text: GroomKit Installation Setting up the GroomKit Maya plugin is a quick and straightforward process. Follow the steps below to perform the initial installation and configure the built-in auto-updater so your XGen grooming workflow always has access to the latest features. Initial Installation Steps Download the latest version of the GroomKit plugin from your personal library on the official Gumroad store. Once downloaded, extract the .zip archive and navigate to the folder that matches your current Autodesk Maya version (e.g., 2027 ). Inside this version folder, click and drag the dragdropinstaller.py script directly into your active Maya window. The script will automatically install the plugin and register the GK shelf in Maya for easy access. To take advantage of the Auto Update feature, open the Check for Update window via GroomKit's top-right menu. Fill in the Email and License Key provided to you at the time of purchase. Using GroomKit Auto-Updater Once your license is linked, you can quickly check for and install future GroomKit updates directly within Maya, eliminating the need to manually re-download files from Gumroad. Auto Update Behavior When updating to the latest release , the plugin will attempt to install the version automatically. In cases where Maya has locked the plugin files in memory, a popup will appear with brief instructions guiding you to the newly downloaded folder so you can use the dragdropinstaller.py script to complete the update manually. Auto-Update Troubleshooting If dragdropinstaller.py raises the following error: Maya has locked the existing files. To resolve this, perform a clean manual installation: Close Maya. Go to Documents/maya/<version>/ (e.g., 2027 ). Delete the scripts/groomkit folder. Delete the plug-ins/groomkitplugin.py file. Restart Maya and drag the installer script in again.

docs.text: XGen Modifiers & SeExpr Library XGen's true power lies in SeExpr —the scripting language it uses to drive procedural variation, masks, and modifiers. While SeExpr is incredibly flexible, remembering exact syntax for randomizing cuts or adding stray hairs can interrupt creative grooming flow. The Expressions tab in GroomKit serves as an interactive SeExpr library of pre-written, high-performance snippets. More than just a text clipboard, GroomKit can automatically build and configure XGen modifiers for you. SeExpr Expression Library GroomKit categorizes SeExpr expressions based on specific grooming needs: Basic Math: Randomize values using Random Sliders, Density Masks, and Random Boolean Masks. XGen Clumping: Advanced setups for cutting hair percentages within clumps or adding procedural noise offsets. Random Noise: Specialized expressions for root noise, flyaways, and stray hair isolation. Wind & Procedural Cuts: Logic for wind direction, structural randomization, and automated hair cutting. Advanced Math: Complex expressions combining IDs, noise patterns, and custom map overrides. For a detailed walkthrough on applying modifiers to your grooming workflow, view our XGen Video Tutorials . The Magic FX Button ✨ The core of the Expressions tab is the fx button , designed to automate the manual setup of XGen modifiers. Instead of manually copying text, clicking the fx button executes a background script that: Creates a new XGen Modifier (e.g., Noise or Cut) within active Description. Configures attributes like Magnitude, Frequency, and Masking directly based on the chosen snippet. Generates and bakes data for Clumping modifiers, automatically processing clumping points and region maps. Example: Automating Flyaway Hair To quickly implement flyaways, locate "Flyaway Noise" under the Random Noise tab and click the fx icon. GroomKit automatically creates the modifier, applies the stray hair SeExpr, sets the Ramp scale, and updates the viewport in one click. Editing & Saving Custom SeExpr Snippets The text fields in GroomKit are fully editable, allowing you to customize math or values for your specific pipeline. Refresh Icon: Restores the snippet to the GroomKit default code. Copy Icon: Copies the SeExpr code to clipboard for manual use in the Maya XGen expression editor. Write expressions to file: Located at the bottom of the UI, this saves your custom modifications to disk. GroomKit will automatically load these tailored expressions in future sessions. docs.text: GroomKit Snippets GroomKit Snippets is a comprehensive collection of automated tools designed for 3D character artists working in Maya. By handling multiple frequently used steps in an automated, repeatable manner, these tools allow artists to work at a higher creative level and focus on adding artistic value to the groom project. XGen Snippets Useful for duplicating XGen descriptions and region mapping. Set Region Map as Guide Color Map: Uses root colors from painted regions to drive guide color. Randomize bounds control shade values for visual separation. Set Region Map as Density Mask: Uses a simple expression to drive density based on painted regions. Duplicate & Setup Description: Duplicates descriptions to new positions while preserving curves and modifiers. Ideal for inheriting modifiers before setting up complex expressions. Reference Usage: Advanced Region - Density mapping . Transfer Snippets Useful for posing characters or moving bounding meshes without using the native Maya Transfer Attributes. Transfer Positions Between Meshes: Easily transfer guide positions by selecting a Source and Target mesh, streamlining the process of moving grooms across geometries. Custom Snippets Provides automated guide placement for an optimal initial layout. Distribute Roots Uniformly: Arranges selected curve/guide roots in a circle, estimating the radius from their initial layout. Apply Modifiers Stack: Create a pre-configured modifiers with customizable number of Clumping, Noises and Cut modifiers. Generate Internal Curves: Interpolates curvature from outer shell guides to a centroid guide to plant new curves. Outputs Maya curves first for stability; click To Guides when satisfied to finalize. Layers count: Number of layers from the outer shell to the centroid. Amount: Total curves generated per layer. Curvature: Curvature influence from outer shell guides. docs.text: GroomKit Tools GroomKit Tools provides a set of curve manipulation utilities designed specifically for hair and fur grooming in Maya. These tools automate common operations such as scattering, shaping, snapping, and transforming multiple curves to streamline the overall grooming workflow. Curve Fill Tools for curves generation within empty spaces or along specific geometries. Tube: Generates a central curve from a cylindrical mesh or scatters curves within a volumetric space defined by selected boundary curves. Card: Generates evenly spaced curves between two boundary curves or across a flat polygon card. Useful for converting polygon hair cards into curve-based grooms. Deform: Offsets curves outward along the underlying mesh surface normals to resolve geometry clipping, utilizing a preserve setting to keep root positions locked in place. Curve Snap Attaches curve roots to the closest point on a designated base mesh. Snap to Base Mesh: Evaluates the root position of selected curves and translates them precisely onto the nearest geometry. Retain & Falloff: Controls the structural preservation of the curve during the snapping process. Retain protects the upper curve shape, while Falloff determines the transition blend from the snapped root into the rest of the strand. Curve Scatter Distributes curves uniformly across a selected mesh based on area-weighted sampling. Reference Curve: Utilizes a designated guide or curve as a structural reference. Generated curves inherit its overall shape and orientation. Smart Distribution: Spatially calculates curve placement based on mesh surface area to prevent dense overlapping, requiring inputs for length, total curve count, and CV count. Symmetry: Mirrors the generated curves across the Object or Global X-axis to establish symmetrical grooming bases. Curve Transform Utilities for selecting and transforming multiple curves in bulk. Random Select: Selects a randomized percentage of curves from the current selection pool based on a slider value. Pivot to Root: Snaps the transform pivot of all selected curves directly to their respective root coordinates. Batch Mode: Configures tools to use local object pivots and smooth soft-selection, enabling simultaneous local scaling or rotation across multiple selected curves. Clump / Spread Modifies the spacing of selected curves by pulling them toward or pushing them away from a central axis. Clump & Spread: Applies an inward (clump) or outward (spread) translation to selected curves based on a Reference curve. If no reference is provided, an average centroid is automatically calculated. Profile Ramp: Dictates the strength and falloff of the clump or spread effect along the length of the curve, from root to tip. Strength: A multiplier for the overall intensity of the clump or spread operation. Workflow Application These tools can be used sequentially. For instance, applying Curve Scatter to generate a base layout, using Curve Transform (Batch Mode) for initial orientation, and applying Clump / Spread for final profile adjustments. .layout-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 4fr 3fr; column-gap: 35px; row-gap: 40px; } @media screen and (max-width: 768px) { .layout-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr !important; column-gap: 15px; row-gap: 10px; margin-bottom: 12px; } .layout-img { margin-top: 0px; } .layout-grid + h2, .layout-grid + h3 { margin-top: 36px; } .layout-grid + h4 { margin-top: 24px; } .rst-footer-buttons a { font-size: 13.5px !important; } }

docs.text: GroomKit Hotkeys Grooming is a highly visual, iterative process. Every time you have to move your mouse away from your character to click a button in the UI, you break your creative flow state. GroomKit provides a comprehensive list of Python commands that mirror its UI functions. By binding these to your keyboard or tablet express keys, you can keep your cursor on your mesh and groom at lightning speed. Auto-registered commands in the Hotkey Editor. Auto Registration In the GroomKit UI under the Hotkeys tab, you will find a Register to Current Hotkeys Set button at the bottom of each category. Clicking this will automatically register all GroomKit commands into your active Maya Hotkey set. You can then open Maya's native Hotkey Editor via Windows > Settings/Preferences > Hotkey Editor , navigate to the Custom Scripts section under the GroomKit category, and easily assign your preferred keys. Single Click: Copy Python command to clipboard. General & Preview Essential viewport and XGen management tools to keep your scene running smoothly. Action Python Command Description XGen Window import groomkit; groomkit.xgen() Opens or focuses the native XGen UI. Update Preview import groomkit; groomkit.preview() Refreshes the generated XGen primitives. Clear Preview import groomkit; groomkit.clear_preview() Clears the generated XGen primitives. Core Sculpting Tools The bread and butter of traditional XGen guide manipulation. Action Python Command Description Sculpt Guides import groomkit; groomkit.sculpt() Standard sculpt brush with selection. Create Guides import groomkit; groomkit.create() Add new guides onto the mesh surface. Normalize Guides import groomkit; groomkit.normalize() Normalize curves cvs spacing. Rebuild Guides import groomkit; groomkit.rebuild() Rebuilds CVs without changing shape. Rebuild Guides (8) import groomkit; groomkit.rebuild(8) Rebuilds guides specifically to 8 CVs. Paste Shape import groomkit; groomkit.shape('paste') Pastes copied shape onto target guides. Lock Length import groomkit; groomkit.lock_length() Preserves guide length during editing. Volumetric Falloff import groomkit; groomkit.volumetric() Toggles a volumetric selection radius. docs.text: GroomKit Profiles: Advanced Operations & XGen Workflow Procedural tube-based grooming workflow across profile types. The Operations section provides a robust suite of utilities for duplicating, mirroring, extracting, and animating your grooming layers. It serves as the central hub for XGen guide binding , macro shaping , and geometry extraction , supporting seamless multi-selection and tag-based filtering for complex Maya grooms. XGen Guides Binding The Guide Binding workflow connects XGen Guides directly to the edges of your procedural profile geometry. This provides a stable, one-click solution for converting procedural hair cards or tubes into guide-driven XGen descriptions. Binding Options: Bind Button: Executes topology-wise extraction and binds XGen guides to the curves. Layers Count: Enables volume-based extraction. This is particularly useful for generating guides that fill the inside area of large hollow tubes. Bake Guides: Bakes the guide positions so they become completely independent from the geometry layer. Remove Button: Removes the bound guides and clears the binding setup from the layer(s). Note: Right-click the Bind Guides button to access the advanced Bind Options menu. Workflow Consistency The Operations frame provides a unified interface that works consistently across all Profile Types (Cards, Tubes, Braids, etc.). Lattice Deformation Using the Maya Lattice Deformer within GroomKit is the most efficient way to adjust the macro shape of your groom. It allows you to modify the silhouette of multiple layers simultaneously, replacing hours of manual curve sculpting. Lattice Options: Lattice Button: Applies a 3x3 Lattice Deformer. Clicking again to accept and bakes the deformation result to the original selection. Preset Buttons: Quick-switch between resolutions ( 2x2 to 5x5 ) for either broad shaping or localized detail tweaks. Duplication & Mirroring GroomKit’s mirroring tools allow you to flip hair geometry across Maya's world space while maintaining all procedural settings. Duplicate Options: New Layer: Choose to create a unique profile layer or merge clones into the existing active layer. Duplicate Button: Clones selected layers while retaining all custom parameter settings and curve ramps. Flip X / Z: Instantly mirrors geometry across the X or Z axis. You can choose to flip the current layer or generate a new mirrored version. Static Geometry Extraction The Extract feature is perfect for baking procedural setups into raw, static Maya geometry—ideal for exporting to game engines, passing to other pipeline, or finalizing a groom. Extraction Options: Extract Checkbox: Automatically groups and organizes all extracted assets within the xgExtract group. Paths Button: Extracts the clean underlying path curves from the selected layers. Edges Button: Generates edge-based curves from the profile geometry (perfect for guide creation). Geometry Button: Converts the procedural profile into standard Maya static meshes. Organized Hierarchy GroomKit ensures consistent naming conventions. Extracted assets are organized under the xgExtract group and named based on their parent layer (e.g., xgCardLayer1_extract ). Pinning to Base Mesh for Animation The Animate Pin feature allows you to attach procedural profiles to a deforming character mesh. Unlike standard guides, GroomKit uses a UV-based node system to bind the layer, ensuring the hair follows the character's movement perfectly during animation. Animate Options: Base Mesh: Attaches to the mesh assigned in the GroomKit Interactive Window. Pin Button: Binds the layer to the UV coordinates of the mesh. The layer indicator turns Red when pinned. Unpin Button: Breaks the binding and registers the curves' current world-space position. Baking Custom Nodes (Curls & Braids) GroomKit uses specialized procedural nodes for Braids and Curls . To ensure your scene renders on machines without GroomKit installed (or for final delivery), use the Bake feature to convert these nodes into standard geometry. Bake Options: Bake Button: Converts procedural curls/braids into static geometry. The indicator turns White . Unbake Button: Reverts the static mesh back into a fully editable procedural GroomKit node. Note: While baked, geometry still follows the path curves but loses localized procedural parameter updates until unbaked. docs.text: GroomKit Profiles: Procedural Hair Geometry for Maya Examples of procedurally generated hair cards, tubes, and braids in Maya. The GroomKit Profiles system is a non-destructive, procedural geometry generator built directly into Maya. Whether you are creating flat Hair Cards for real-time game engines, stylized Tubes, or complex Braids, Profiles allow you to drive heavy geometry using simple and lightweight path curves. This feature combines geometry shaping, curve extraction, and guide binding into a single, intuitive workflow. By keeping your entire grooming process inside Maya, GroomKit eliminates the need for external software, allowing artists to stay focused on creative styling. Profiles Window & UI Structure GroomKit Profiles utilizes a Layer-based workflow . By grouping guide curves into a Layer and assigning a Profile type, GroomKit automatically generates the corresponding mesh. Because the system is fully procedural, you can modify your curves using Interactive Sculpting Tools , and the generated geometry will update in real-time. The Profiles interface is organized into four main sections for efficient groom management: Profile Types: Toggle between 5 distinct generation types: Hair Cards , Tubes , Twists , Curls , and Braids . Layers & Tags Management : Organize and tag your groom layers. Supports multi-selection and context-menu operations. Layer Operations: Utility tools for grooming, including Bind Guides, Lattice Deform, Duplicate, and Geometry Extraction. Layer Settings: Procedural controls for the mesh. Use sliders and curve ramps to adjust scale, rotation, frequency, and width dynamically. Layers & Tags Management The Layers UI is the primary dashboard for your groom. It is custom-built to handle complex tasks such as visibility toggling, geometry operations, and viewport color-coding for better scene organization. Essential Layer Controls Every layer provides instant access to these essential grooming toggles: 1. Layer Indicator: Access advanced functions to pin or bake a layer. 2. Layer Name: Auto-assigned name for the procedural layer. 3. Layer Color: Set a custom viewport display color for easy identification. 4. Layer Tag: Categorize layers using a 3-letter tagging system. 5. Visibility Button: Cycle display modes: Visible (V) , Hidden (H) , Template (T) , and Path (P) . 6. Color Bucket: Randomize viewport colors across selected layers. 7. Geometry Icon: Manage bound Guides or select the XGen Description. 8. Remove Button: Safely delete the layer while preserving original curves in the xgCurves group. 9. Auto Select: Automatically highlights layers in the UI based on your Maya viewport selection. 10. Master Controls: Global toggles that affect all layers simultaneously. Performance Note: Auto Select Toggle off Auto Select when not in active use. Leaving it enabled causes GroomKit to constantly query the viewport for selections, which may impact performance in heavy scenes. Cycling between display modes and procedural layer colors. Layer Context Menu Right-click any layer name to access management functions for duplicating or transferring settings between layers. Quick access to core management actions: Edit Layer: Open detailed procedural parameters. Copy/Paste Layer: Transfer all parameters and curve ramps between layers. Duplicate Layer: Create an exact replica of the layer and its settings. Delete Layer: Remove the procedural setup from the scene. Layer Geometry Menu Right-click the Geometry Icon (grid/sphere) to access tools for geometry extraction, animation prep, and XGen guide utilities. Specialized tools for interacting with the generated mesh: Snap Layer: Conform the layer's guides to the character's surface. Extract Layer: Convert procedural data into standard Maya polygons. Animate Layer: Setup the groom for dynamic simulation or character rigging. For layers bound to XGen guides , additional utilities are available: Hide/Select Guides: Quickly manage guide visibility to reduce clutter. Select Description: Locate the tied XGen Description node in the Outliner. Multi-Scene Workflow The Copy-Paste function works globally across different Maya instances. docs.text: Interactive Tools for Maya Curves & XGen Guides The Interactive Tools module is the core of GroomKit's fluid 3D grooming workflow. It provides a unified, brush-based toolset designed to work seamlessly with both native Maya Curves Sculpting and XGen Guides Brushes without manual context-switching required. Base Mesh (Crucial) Before using the Interactive tools, it's generally better to assign the Base Mesh for predictable behavior. This tells GroomKit which surface the curves and guides belong to, allowing the tools to calculate accurate surface snapping, normal orientation, and root locking correctly. When a geometry is set, the tools will exclusively reference this mesh and ignore operations on other background geometries. Select your character's scalp or body geometry. Click the Set Mesh button in the Interactive menu. Enable, Disable, and Clear You can temporarily disable surface snapping without losing your mesh assignment. Right-click the Set Mesh button to reveal a popup menu where you can Enable/Disable the active mesh, or Clear it entirely. Interactive Radial Menu For optimal layout efficiency, the Interactive Tools menu functions as a detachable floating panel. Click Detach Interactive Window in the top-right menu to position your brushes adjacent to your 3D workspace, leaving the main window open for other interfaces. You can also access the toolset instantly by registering it as a Radial Marking Menu (Ctrl + Shift + MMB) or by using the complete suite of tool-specific Maya hotkeys. 🖌️ Interactive Toolset The Tool Settings frame will update accordingly to the selected tool context. Sculpt Brush Multifunction tools for curve sculpting and profile shaping. Add Brush Quickly populate empty areas by drawing new curves directly on the surface. Cut Brush A fluid, slide-to-cut tool. Click and drag left/right on a curve to trim its length dynamically. Draw Brush Draw freehand curves on the screen plane or directly onto the Base Mesh. Attach Brush Click and drag to connect two curve segments or adjust an existing attachment. Move Brush Slide existing curves or guides fluidly across the surface of the Base Mesh without altering their original shape. Important Note Avoid using the Undo command (Ctrl + Z) while generating or duplicating XGen guides. This action triggers an unavoidable limitation that causes Maya to crash. docs.text: Misc Utilities: Advanced Shaping & Workflows The Misc Utilities section contains some of GroomKit's most powerful and workflow-accelerating features. This section bridges the gap between manual sculpting and procedural generation, offering tools for clumping maps, advanced deformations, and universal curve extensions. Using Base Mesh as target for Snapping workflow. Standard Shaping Tools Target Guides Tool Quickly access XGen / Utilities / Target Tool, useful in creating clumping guides. Set Target: Makes the selected guide a target. Move Guides: Move selecting guides toward the targeted guide. Clean Up: Removes target sphere from the scene. Curve/Guide Extrude Extends hair naturally by calculating the path and adding a new control point at the tip, preserving the shape. Universal: Works with both Maya NURBS Curves and XGen Guides. Fine control: Provides exact control for shaping hair buns or curls. Customize Your Hotkeys To optimize your grooming experience, almost all operations in the GroomKit menu can be assigned to custom hotkeys for a faster, uninterrupted workflow. Automated Workflows Speed up your blockout phase with faster guide placement and real-time visual feedback. Conform/Snap Workflow Shape your silhouette quickly by snapping guides directly to a reference mesh—no need to worry about the underlying blockout topology. Conform/Snap Button: Snap your selected guides down onto the surface. Magnet Icon: Automatically use your Base Mesh as the snap target. Set Target: Pick any custom mesh in your scene to snap guides to. Live Mirror By dynamically reflecting mirrored guide positions across the X-axis, this feature provides a better grooming experience with instant feedback Mirror Button: Generate a static, one-time mirrored copy. Live Mirror: Mirror your guide edits instantly in real-time. Toggle Mirror: Hide mirrored guides and show simple gray proxies. Check Integrity: Scan and fix broken elements to maintain stability. Bake Position: Lock in final positions and clear out setup nodes. Discard: Delete the mirror setup and clean the node history. 🔧 Advanced Shaping Tools Include toolset to manipulate both curves and guides in changing macro and micro CV control points Applying 3x3 lattice deformer. Lattice Deformer Easily adjust the overall volume of your groom without losing your detailed sculpt work. This tool works seamlessly across XGen guides, Maya curves, and procedurally generated braids . Select a group of guides or curves. Division: Set the deformer resolution using the slider (e.g., 3x3x3). Shaping: Click Lattice and move the control points to shape selecting curves. Applying: Click Lattice again to apply the result. (Optional): Right-click the button for quick access to Accept, Cancel, and Preference options. Smooth & Relax Perfect for cleaning up jittery mouse strokes and softening the flow of your hair. Smooth: Removes sudden bumps and noise without shrinking the overall length of the hair. Relax: Creates beautiful, natural arcs. Higher values will gently pull a squiggly curve into a clean, sweeping C shape. docs.text: Sculpt Settings: Core Grooming Tools XGen The Sculpt panel is your primary hub for foundational 3D character grooming operations. Whether you are manipulating native Autodesk Maya Curves or XGen Guides , GroomKit unifies these actions into a single, intuitive interface, keeping your focus on the viewport rather than technical menus. Quick access using XGen buttons. XGen Viewport Buttons At the very top of the Sculpt tab, you will find three essential buttons with added functionality for rapidly managing XGen guide display directly in the Maya viewport. Right-click on the Preview or Clear buttons to access the corresponding context menus containing essential viewport and guide management functions. The XGen button serves as a quick shortcut to access and manage the main XGen workspace alongside GroomKit. Click: Open the native XGen Window. Double Click: Close all tabs and resize the GroomKit window. The Preview button allows you to generate interpolation previews for your hair descriptions, as well as easily reveal and unlock guides. Click: Toggle description preview. Double Click: Preview all descriptions. Right Click Menu: Show collections guides, Show description guides, Unlock description guides The Clear button provides options to remove generated hair previews, as well as hide or lock guides to declutter your viewport. Click: Clear description preview. Double Click: Clear previews for all descriptions. Right Click Menu: Hide collections guides, Hide description guides, Lock description guides Selection Tip You can enable Auto Select to quickly switch between XGen descriptions right in the viewport. General Grooming Settings The Settings foldout contains the standard operations you'll use constantly while shaping your hair and fur grooms. Sculpt Modifier Settings Lock Length: Locks hair length while sculpting to prevent accidental stretching and maintain volume. 3D Volumetric: Uses a 3D brush sphere to select only nearby hair, preventing accidental grabs on the opposite side of the head. Quick access to Tool Settings checkboxes. Base Sculpting Tools All buttons are applicable for both XGen guides and Maya curves, depending on your current selection. Sculpt: Activates the default Maya/XGen sculpting context. (Note: For advanced grooming, see Interactive Tools ). Create: Activates the Add Primitives tool to plant guides on the mesh. Copy / Paste Shape: Select a source guide and click Copy , then select target guides and click Paste to instantly transfer the exact curvature. Normalize Curves The Normalize tool redistributes the Control Vertices (CVs) of your selected curves or guides evenly along their length. Maintaining clean curve data is essential for a smooth and predictable groom. Rebuild Resolution Rebuilding allows you to change the resolution (CV count) of your guides or curves while preserving their original shape , distributing the new CVs evenly along the curve's length. Rebuild Slider: Manually dial in the exact number of CVs you want. Quick Presets (8, 16, 24): Instantly rebuild selected curves to common resolutions with a single click. Hotkey Commands You can bind these core functions to your Maya Hotkeys (Windows > Settings/Preferences > Hotkey Editor). Make sure the language is set to Python for these scripts to work. docs.text: Maya Curves Utilities The Curves utilities foldout is a powerhouse for hair translation in Maya. Whether you are building a groom from proxy geometry or simply need to manage native Maya curves before converting them into XGen guides , this section provides everything required to extract, clean, and convert your curve data efficiently. One-click curve extraction from existing hair assets Extract Curves from Edges Select a contiguous edge loop on a polygon mesh. GroomKit will rip it off and convert it into a clean, rebuilt NURBS curve. Available options: CVs Count : controls extracted curves resolution Extract Selected generates curves directly from the selected contiguous edge loops. Extract Curves from Cards Select flat polygonal hair cards to serve as the proxy geometry. You can dictate exactly where the curves are generated along the card's surface. Available options: CVs Count : controls extracted curves resolution Curves Count : controls the number of extracted curves Extract Center extracts a single, perfect core curve running down the middle of the card. Extract Sides extracts two curves along the outer boundaries of the card. Extract Shell extracts a perimeter of curves wrapped around the surface. You control the density with the Curves Count slider. Extract Curves from Tubes Select 3D cylindrical hair meshes. GroomKit analyzes the volume of the tubes to generate core, surface, or concentric interior curves. Available options: CVs Count : controls extracted curves resolution Curves Count : controls the number of extracted curves Layers Count : controls the number of extracted layers Extract Center extracts a single, perfect core curve running down the middle of the tube. Extract Shell extracts a perimeter of curves wrapped around the surface. You control the density with the Curves Count slider. Extract Layers generates concentric rings of curves inside the volume of the tube. Controlled by the Layers Count slider. Additional Extraction Options Once you have chosen your extraction method, GroomKit offers several additional options and parameters to refine the resolution, organization, and orientation of the generated Maya curves. Option Description Hide Meshes Automatically hides the original proxy geometry after extraction to organize your viewport. Merge Curves Groups all extracted curves into a single, clean xgExtract group in the Outliner. Flip Direction Reverses the U/V calculation if your curves are generating sideways. Procedural Workflow Currently, to make use of the curve extraction engine, it's required your proxy geometry is standard and has extractable topology. Estimated curve extraction may be implemented in future versions. Further more, GroomKit Profiles support non-destructive tube-based grooming, allowing you to block out your character's hair, extract it to guides, and shape them procedurally for complex XGen hairstyles without ever leaving Maya. Topology Note Set the CVs Count slider to 0 to inherit the exact CV count from source geometry. General Maya Curve Operations Quick utilities to sanitize your curve data before groom generation. Toggle CVs: Instantly shows or hides the Control Vertices of the selected curves without digging into Maya's display menus. Reverse Curves: Reverses the root-to-tip direction of the curve. (Crucial: XGen assumes the first CV is the root. If your hair is growing into the head, use this!) Select Roots: Automatically selects the first CV ( cv[0] ) of all currently selected curves. Rebuild Curves: Opens Maya's native Rebuild Curve options for manual tweaking. Toggle Curve CVs. Select Roots and Reverse Curves. Convert Maya Curves to XGen Guides Instead of navigating nested UI layers in the standard XGen window, you can swiftly execute the curve-to-guide conversion directly from this panel using the following options: Delete: Automatically deletes the original Maya curves after guide generation. Dynamic Link (Preserve): Maintains the source Maya curves and creates a procedural link, ensuring XGen guides inherit any subsequent edits. Add Guides: Executes the conversion based on your current configuration. Insert XGen guides using GroomKit interface. Hotkey Commands Bind these to your hotkeys (Python mode) to speed up your extraction and conversion workflow. Curves Commands Extract Curves (Uses current UI settings): import groomkit; groomkit.extract.extract_curves() Reverse Selected Curves: import groomkit; groomkit.curves.reverse_curves() Select Roots: import groomkit; groomkit.curves.select_roots() Convert Curves to Guides: import groomkit; groomkit.curves.to_guides() .layout-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 4fr 3fr; column-gap: 35px; row-gap: 40px; } .layout-content { margin-bottom: -32px; } .layout-img { margin-top: 45px; } @media screen and (max-width: 768px) { .layout-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr !important; column-gap: 15px; row-gap: 10px; margin-bottom: 12px; } .layout-img { margin-top: 0px; } .layout-grid + h2, .layout-grid + h3 { margin-top: 36px; } .layout-grid + h4 { margin-top: 24px; } .layout-content { margin-bottom: 0px; } .layout-content +div { margin-top: 20px; } } .items-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; column-gap: 35px; row-gap: 30px; align-items: start; } @media screen and (max-width: 768px) { .items-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } }

docs.text: XGen Guides Utilities The Guides foldout focuses on structural adjustments to native XGen guides to streamline your 3D hair grooming workflow. It includes dedicated tools for snapping floating hair back to the scalp, securely moving roots and tips without breaking the groom, and cleaning up intersecting spline data. Auto Select XGen Description Maximize your 3D grooming workspace by handling tasks outside the standard XGen windows. Enabling Auto Select XGen Description instantly identifies and switches to the corresponding setting for any guides or curves clicked in the viewport, reducing long trips using manual dropdown navigation. The Auto Select toggle can now be found in the Utils tab (as of v1.0.0). Clumping Automation Centralizes map generation controls, allowing you to generate maps for multiple clumping modifiers simultaneously via: The Generate Clumping Maps button. The Clumping Option inside the Interactive Menu . Indicator Icons Description Condition Indicator Warning - No clump guides found. Map uninitialized Guide-based - Generated from native XGen guides. Density = 1.0 Generate-based - Generated across the mesh surface. Density ≠ 1.0 Clumping Points Set Density to 1.0 for Guide-based maps, and any other value for Generate-based maps. Move Guide Roots Easily adjust root positions without shifting the rest of the guide. This localized spline manipulation is crucial for refining masks, regions, and overall clumping. The Move Root workflow lets you reposition root CVs while preserving the guide's original shape. Root Toggle: Click to temporarily convert the guide to a curve and unlock the root. Move it, then click again to apply changes and revert to a guide. Organizing guide roots toward the center part line. Move Guide Tips Define the final hair silhouette and flow by repositioning the ends of the guides without affecting the overall spline shape. The Move Tip workflow lets you adjust tip CVs while keeping the rest of the guide intact. Tip Toggle: Click to temporarily convert the guide to a curve and unlock the tip. Move it, then click again to apply changes and revert to a guide. Changing hair shape by moving tips. Curve-to-Guide Switch Seamlessly toggle selections between XGen guides and native Maya curves. This lets you leverage the best sculpting tools from both workflows simultaneously. Switch Toggle: Instantly convert guides to curves (or vice versa). Excellent for applying tools like localized curve smoothing directly to the guides. Accessible Hotkeys The Root , Tip , and Switch buttons are designed to be called repeatedly during the grooming workflow. Assigning them to custom hotkeys is highly recommended to build muscle memory and avoid UI menu diving. Guide Overlap Check & Conversion Heavy grooms easily hide accidental duplicates, causing XGen clumping math to explode. GroomKit lets you quickly isolate overlapping guides, or convert them back to curves for advanced deformations. Distance Threshold: Defines the proximity for overlapping guides. docs.text: XGen Hair Shaders Assigning and tweaking hair materials in Maya's XGen can be a tedious process involving the Hypershade and hunting down specific shading nodes. GroomKit's Shaders module acts as an instant material library and procedural variation engine for fast viewport look-dev. GroomKit Hair Shaders. Applying Hair Shader Presets GroomKit ships with several built-in realtime hair shader presets, while also offering full support for creating your own custom palettes. Color Swatches: Previews the Root, Tip, and Primary Highlight colors of the preset. Clicking on them focuses the Attribute Editor. Apply Button: Applies the shader preset to the active XGen description. Var Button: Applies procedural clump-based color variation on top of the shader preset. Double-Click: Cascades the shader preset or variation to all descriptions in the current collection. Shader presets are highly configurable and highly reusable between projects. Users can either use the built-in library or create new custom shaders that can be applied with just a single click. Applying shaders in real-time viewport. Customization While the built-in presets provided by GroomKit serve simply as a starting point, the true power of the Shader module lies in its flexibility. Users are encouraged to create their own custom shader presets to aid in look-dev during the grooming process. Shader Preset Breakdown A preset row is a quick preview of the hair material to be applied to your XGen description. It provides immediate functionality through buttons and color swatches. Preset Name: The name of the hair shader preset (either built-in or user-generated). Color Swatches: A brief preview of the root, tip, and highlight colors. Clicking any of these will open and focus the connected hair shader material in the Attribute Editor for customization. Apply Button: Applies the preset to the currently active XGen description. Var Button: Adds a procedural expression on top of the shader to produce clump-based color variation. (Double Click): Double-clicking either Apply or Var will execute the action across all descriptions in the currently active XGen collection. Right Mouse Click: Right-clicking the preset name allows you to restore a built-in preset to its factory default, or delete a user-created preset entirely. Procedural Hair Color Variation (Var) Perfectly uniform hair color can look synthetic. Real hair has micro-variations in lightness and darkness on a per-strand basis. The Var (Variation) button injects a complex procedural noise expression into XGen's GLRenderer, giving you viewport sliders to control the chaos. Applying clump-based color variation. Once applied, you can adjust these properties in the XGen Editor Window under the Preview/Output > Primitive Color tab: Freq (Frequency): Controls the scale and density of the variation noise. Lower values create larger, broader patches of grouped colors. Higher values generate finer, more chaotic, strand-by-strand detail. Seed: Changes the random starting point of the noise pattern. Adjust this to quickly shuffle the variation layout without changing the scale. Min: Defines the darkest lightness value/multiplier of the color variation. Max: Defines the brightest lightness value/multiplier of the color variation. (Note: To clear the variation and return to a flat color, right-click the Var button and select "Clear", or simply re-click the Apply button.) How to Create Custom Hair Shaders Advanced Customization The provided shaders might not always give the exact look you're looking for. Because of this, we encourage you to experiment with the shader parameters to match your vision and understand how they work. Hair shaders in GroomKit are grouped into two categories: hairPhysicalShader: Maya's standard viewport-friendly shader that comes natively with XGen descriptions. aiStandardHair: Arnold's realism-based shader featuring advanced highlight, transmission, and melanin controls. Customizing: Apply a preset, then click any of its Color Swatches to instantly focus the Attribute Editor on that exact active shader node. Customize Maya hairPhysicalShader Click to expand configuration parameters... The hairPhysicalShader is great for fast viewport look-dev and stylized grooms. Root / Tip Color: Drives the primary base color gradient of the hair strand. Diffuse Weight: Controls how strongly the Root and Tip colors are displayed. A value of 0 means the hair is entirely driven by highlights. Primary / Secondary Highlight Color: Drives the color and tint of the hair's gloss and shine. Other Parameters: Attributes like Scatter , Shift , and Transmission offer subtle stylistic changes to the visual effect and can generally be left at default for standard looks. Customize Arnold aiStandardHair Click to expand configuration parameters... The aiStandardHair is Arnold's physically accurate hair model, relying on melanin rather than simple diffuse colors. Melanin & Melanin Redness: The primary driver for realistic hair. 0.0 yields blonde/white hair, while 1.0 yields black hair. Melanin Redness adds auburn/ginger tones. Roughness: Controls the sharpness of the specular highlight. Lower values create shiny/glossy hair, while higher values create dry/matte hair. Specular Tints: Allows you to tint the natural white highlights with specific colors (great for faking colored lighting or dyed reflections). Diffuse Color & Weight: Used specifically for dyed, painted, or stylized hair. Increasing the diffuse weight overrides the natural Melanin calculation with the chosen Diffuse Color. Saving Custom Shader Presets Once you have tweaked a shader in the Attribute Editor to your liking, you can save it to GroomKit for future use. There are two ways to do this: 1. Automated Method (Override existing preset) If you are tweaking a preset that is already applied from the GroomKit UI, GroomKit tracks it. Simply click the Apply button on that same preset row again. GroomKit will detect the changes and automatically overwrite the preset file with your new settings. 2. Manual Method (Create new preset) If you want to save your tweaks as an entirely new preset without overwriting an old one: Ensure the Attribute Editor is focused on your active hairPhysicalShader or aiStandardHair . Click the Presets* button at the top right of the Attribute Editor. Select Save [Node] Preset... and give it a name. In the GroomKit Shaders UI, click the large Reload all Hair Shader Presets button. A new material will instantly appear in the User Presets section! (Removing built-in presets) Saving custom hair shader. Restoring Shader Presets Right-click the name of any built-in shader preset and select Reset to restore its colors and parameters back to factory defaults. Right-clicking a User Preset will allow you to Delete it. .layout-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 3fr 2fr; column-gap: 35px; row-gap: 40px; } @media screen and (max-width: 768px) { .layout-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr !important; column-gap: 15px; row-gap: 10px; margin-bottom: 12px; } .layout-img { margin-top: 0px; } .layout-grid + h2, .layout-grid + h3 { margin-top: 36px; } .layout-grid + h4 { margin-top: 24px; } }

docs.text: Simulation Shaping GroomKit enables gravity draping to aid manual hair sculpting by wiring up curve-guide shaping to Maya's simulation engine-driven physics. The Simulation module temporarily wraps your curves in Maya's Nucleus physics engine. This enables dynamic draping, accurate mesh collisions, and streamlines baking the simulation results back into the original XGen guides . Hair Simulation Setup Use the Simulation module to quickly conform strands to reference geometry using natural physics. Simulate: Automatically builds the physics rig and begins simulating selected guides. Acts as a play/pause toggle. Rewind (Simulate RMB): Rolls the timeline back to the start position. Clean Up: Discards the simulation data and removes the physics stack. Apply: Bakes the simulation result to selected guides and removes the physics stack. Simulate XGen guides and preview update. Apply Collision: Select your target geometry (body/head) and click this to generate an nRigid collider. This prevents simulation pass-through and ensures hair correctly collides with the character's surface. Simulate with collision object. Advanced Gravity Controls Adjust gravity parameters of physics solver for customized results. Apply Collision: Assign additional meshes to block the simulation. Gravity Sliders: Modify the global force (G) and vector direction (X, Y, Z) to simulate gravity or wind pulls. Retain Sliders: Blend the simulation with your original sculpt to prevent volume collapse at the roots. Nucleus*: Access the native Maya attribute editor for global physical settings. Partially Simulate For realistic draping that maintains base volume, set the Retain slider to 60-70% . This preserves your manual sculpt at the roots while simulating the lower lengths. Simulation also applicable for procedurally generated geometry. Maya nHair System & Nucleus Native Maya physics attributes (Stiffness, Damping, Wind Control) are highly technical and often tedious to balance. GroomKit applies optimized defaults in the background, making direct adjustment of these node attributes unnecessary for standard grooming tasks. Info Detailed documentation for simulation setup will be provided in a future update. Scene Stability Directly sliding the Time Slider backwards can cause solver instability. Always utilize the Rewind button (Right-Click Simulate) to revert simulations safely.
